reviews.one_line_contribution: A 2x2 provenance crossover in ALFWorld in which a GEPA-optimized instruction and a distilled experience bank are each built from the same training episodes but labelled by which three of the six task types produced them, so that the amount of a memory bank's task-specific value already absorbed by the instruction can be read off the instruction-provenance x bank-provenance interaction at matched test type, with an information-free best-of-w sampling ladder used to subtract the headroom compression that the accuracy gap between the two instructions would produce mechanically.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, jointly. (a) MIPROv2 (2406.11695): its instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint ablation is exactly the two-container question, and its published finding that the split is task-dependent already supplies the qualitative answer this proposal seeks; what the proposal adds over it is retrieval, distillation, token matching and the provenance labelling, which is a sharper instrument for a question whose direction is known. (b) EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) as the proposal itself reports it: ReasoningBank +3.6 vs GEPA +1.2 on shared 528/267 trajectories on Qwen3.5-27B is already the headline that an optimizer on the same episodes gets roughly what the bank gets. The proposal is candid that this sentence is in the literature and cites it as motivation. Neither work manipulates provenance or puts an optimizer and a bank in the same context, so novelty is not extinguished, but what remains is a measurement refinement of an accepted qualitative claim, not a new phenomenon. Experience Distillation (2607.21051) is a third threat on the quantity itself: retains >=64.8% of an in-context gain in a second container is the same retention-ratio result with weights rather than an instruction as the rival container.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory threshold is arithmetically incompatible with the gate that licenses it. Delta_abs = [Inner(I_oth) - Inner(I_own)] - ladder correction, and the ladder correction is positive by the proposal's own argument (I_own sits above I_oth in level, so compression makes D positive mechanically). If Inner(I_own) >= 0, which is what the absorption hypothesis rather than the interference hypothesis predicts, then Delta_abs <= Inner(I_oth) - correction. G3 only requires the relevance advantage to clear 4pt with a lower CI of 1pt, and Inner(I_oth) is measured at an optimized instruction, i.e. at a level at or above I0 where compression is if anything worse. So a Delta_abs of 5pt requires the on-type bank's advantage to be essentially annihilated and then some at I_own, while the design admits itself into the confirmatory stage on a 4pt advantage. Under the gate's own floor the effect the study claims to be powered for cannot occur, and a real, substantial partial absorption of, say, 40% of a 5pt advantage is 2pt, far below both the 5pt threshold and the 4.6-4.8pt MDE, and would be reported as inconclusive. The modal realized outcome of this design is therefore a bounded null on the primary, and the paper falls back on secondary endpoints that are much closer to what EvoAgentBench and MIPROv2 already show. Two supporting design gaps sharpen this. First, there is no gate on the instruction-provenance main effect (cells 8 vs 9), even though the proposal correctly states that an instruction that learned nothing type-specific cannot have absorbed anything type-specific; GEPA on ALFWorld plausibly buys generic scaffolding (action syntax, receptacle enumeration, re-prompt discipline) that transfers across all six types, in which case the square is guaranteed null before it is run, and G0-G5 will not catch it. Second, ladder B, which Risk Factor 3 names as the direct test of the one-dimensionality assumption the entire headroom correction rests on, is third on the Tier-0 contingency cut list, ahead of reducing optimizer seeds and ahead of reducing n; the pre-registered degradation path deletes the validation of the primary statistic while keeping the statistic.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Re-derive the gate from the endpoint instead of setting them independently. G3 should require a dev relevance advantage of roughly 10-12pt, not 4pt, or the primary should be restated as an absorbed fraction 1 - Inner(I_own)/Inner(I_oth) with a threshold on the ratio and the design powered for the ratio's delta-method CI, which is currently only a descriptive quantity. Add a gate on the instruction-provenance main effect, acc(I_own x M0) - acc(I_oth x M0) > 0 with a lower CI above zero on S_dev2, and branch to the level-based endpoint if it fails, since the square is uninterpretable without it. Move ladder B off the cut list and cut n or the third optimizer seed instead. Decompose Inner(I) into its help component acc(I x B_own) - acc(I x M0) and its harm component acc(I x M0) - acc(I x B_oth) using cells 8 and 9, and pre-register that absorption requires the help component to shrink: as written, a shrinking Inner at I_own is equally consistent with the optimized instruction making the agent more robust to irrelevant injected text, which is distractor-robustness rather than content transfer, and the fix/break 2/3 rule does not separate the two. Finally, add a direct content check the design currently lacks entirely: a textual overlap or ablation analysis showing that I_own actually contains the procedures that B_own's items encode. The claim in the title is about content moving between containers, and the whole plan tests only a behavioral interaction.
reviews.missing_baseline: I_all: an instruction optimized on the union of both type sets, crossed with {M0, B_own, B_oth} on S_test. Every cell of the square uses an instruction optimized on only half the task space, which is a configuration no practitioner would deploy, yet predictions 5 and 6 are stated as the practitioner's number and as a deployment recommendation to compile once and drop retrieval. I1_all appears only in cell 20, at Tier 1, with 2 seeds on the 274-game official splits, which is badly underpowered for the 3pt bounds those predictions use and is cuttable. A reviewer will say the deployment claim is made in a condition never measured at power. Secondary omission with the same character: the long-context dump baselines M_all and R_raw are Tier 1, although the proposal itself cites EvoMemBench for long-context baselines remaining highly competitive against 15 memory methods, and AutoMEM for a flat-file harness beating eight of them; if raw dumping matches the bank, the container framing loses its second container before absorption is even at issue.
reviews.preprint_collision: Process is well above what proposals in this area usually show: two dated scans, 15 HuggingFace queries over 244 papers, by-id abstract verification for 54 IDs, a committed litscan table with the rule that no cited ID is absent from it, EvoAgentBench read from the PDF with a committed SHA256, and a self-correction of a web snippet that had misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 against the PDF's +3.6, plus reinstatement of five IDs wrongly retracted in v2. I credit that. But the check does not establish novelty, by the proposal's own accounting. The only thing claimed as new is the use of the provenance crossover as the identification of container substitution, and obligation (2), the targeted search of the prompt-optimization, contamination and data-attribution literatures for held-out-episode and data-provenance crossovers, has never been run from this node. An unsearched claim is a weakness: crossover designs of exactly this shape are routine in data attribution and in contamination auditing, and the odds that no 2026 preprint has applied one to a prompt optimizer or a memory bank are not low. Obligation (1), the unopened appendix of 2608.14036, is acknowledged as the collision that would gut prediction 6, and obligation (3), cross-task-type transfer of procedural memory in the embodied-agent literature, targets precisely the type-set manipulation the instrument is built on. Also material: arXiv is unreachable from the node, so every load-bearing 2026 ID rests on web-search snippets through a single channel. I can independently confirm only the pre-2026 anchors, and those are accurate as characterized (ExpeL 2308.10144, A-MEM 2502.12110, Memp 2508.06433, GEPA 2507.19457 with its >10% over MIPROv2 and ~35x rollout claim, MIPROv2 2406.11695, ReasoningBank 2509.25140), which is a real credibility signal; the 2026 IDs, including MemHarness 2607.28272 whose 70.1/76.4/85.2 numbers carry the premise that ALFWorld memory effects are 5-15 points, I cannot verify and neither, on one channel, can the authors. No preprint I know of makes this exact claim, so I do not find a hard collision; I find a novelty claim that the submission itself marks conditional on searches not yet performed, and that is how I have scored it.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A 2x2 provenance crossover in ALFWorld in which a retrieved procedural-experience bank and a GEPA-optimized instruction are each labelled by which three ALFWorld task types' episodes produced them, so that 'how much of the bank's task-specific value an optimized instruction has already absorbed' is read off the instruction-provenance x bank-provenance interaction (Delta_abs), with a headroom correction fitted along an information-free best-of-w sampling ladder.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202) and MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695) jointly. EvoAgentBench already puts a retriever (ReasoningBank, +3.6) and GEPA (+1.2) on the same 528/267 training trajectories across four domains and three backbones, which is exactly the proposal's qualitative headline -- an optimizer given the same episodes gets roughly what the bank gets -- and the proposal concedes this in Related Work section 3 ('already in the literature; we cite it as motivation rather than claiming it'). MIPROv2's instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint ablation is the two-container question itself, with the finding that the split is task-dependent, which pre-empts the qualitative answer. Neither is a full collision: EvoAgentBench has no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell and no provenance manipulation, and MIPROv2 has no retrieval. But together they leave the residual novelty as a design device (the provenance labelling) whose primitive the proposal itself declines to claim, plus one environment's measurement. A reviewer will ask what the interaction buys beyond a table that is already published, and the answer is a second-order statistic with SE 1.85pt.
reviews.strongest_objection: The identification rests entirely on the ladder correction, and the ladder under-corrects in the direction of the hypothesis, so Delta_abs > 5pt is reachable with zero content transfer between containers. Inner(I) = acc(I x B_own) - acc(I x B_oth) does hold the residual unsolved set constant within one instruction, but Delta_abs compares Inner at I_own against Inner at I_oth and repairs the level gap with Inner_H fitted on ladder A (cell 10, best-of-w action sampling, w in {2,4,8}). Best-of-w raises accuracy by resolving games lost to sampling noise; an on-type optimized instruction raises accuracy by resolving games lost to missing type-specific procedure -- precisely the games the on-type bank is there to fix. So at matched no-memory accuracy the ladder leaves the type-specific-fixable games unsolved while I_own has already removed them, Inner_H(l_own) stays high while Inner(I_own) collapses, and the difference is scored as absorption. The residual-unsolved-set objection that the proposal says 'cannot be raised against' its endpoint has not been eliminated; it has been moved out of the primary contrast and into the correction term, where it is confounded with the effect rather than orthogonal to it. Ladder B (step budget, cell 11) does not test this: it is a second generic knob, and generic-vs-generic agreement is uninformative about generic-vs-targeted mismatch. Compounding this, Delta_abs is not the claim in the title. A large Delta_abs says the *type-specific* slice of the bank's value shrinks; the practitioner-relevant assertion that 'the bank stops paying at an optimized instruction' is g(I_own, B_own), which is demoted to secondary endpoint (c)/prediction 5 with a +/-1.5-1.9pt bounded-loss CI. The paper's headline therefore rests on a secondary quantity while the confirmatory endpoint is an interaction that does not entail it.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add the arm that separates episode provenance from task-type provenance: an instruction I_own' optimized on a P_train-disjoint pool of the *same* three task types, evaluated against B_own and B_oth. If Inner(I_own') is as depressed as Inner(I_own), the effect is 'the instruction learned the task type', not 'the instruction absorbed these episodes', and the 'same training episodes, two containers' framing that the title asserts is dead. As written, P_train is shared by both containers by design, so the square cannot make this distinction at all. (2) Fix the partition or measure it first. T_A = {pick_two, clean, look_in_light} and T_B = {pick_and_place, cool, heat} split the near-isomorphic pairs across sets: clean/cool/heat are the same find-object -> apply-appliance -> place skeleton, and pick_two/pick_and_place differ by a repetition. The partition was chosen by game counts, which maximizes cross-type transfer and therefore minimizes the relevance advantage G3 needs. Worse, G1 (g(I0,B_own) >= 5pt) and G3 (g_own - g_oth >= 4pt) together require the off-type bank to be worth <= 1pt in an environment where all six types share one action space and one receptacle-search procedure. Measure cross-type transfer on S_dev before committing, or partition by procedural similarity ({pick_and_place, pick_two, look_in_light} vs {clean, cool, heat}). Otherwise the modal outcome is the G3 branch, whose primary is the level-ladder endpoint the proposal says four rounds of reviewers already rejected. (3) Replace or supplement ladder A with a *targeted* level control -- e.g. instructions produced by subsampling the on-type optimizer's rollout budget, giving a level ladder that moves accuracy the same way the treatment does -- and pre-register a sensitivity analysis stating how much of Delta_abs survives if the correction under-corrects by a stated fraction. (4) Promote g(I_own, B_own) to co-primary. (5) Discharge pre-freeze obligation (2) before submission, not before freeze. (6) Republish the call budget: ~15 calls/episode is inconsistent with G0's own 20-60% timeout rate at L0 in 20-30 (timeouts always spend the full budget), and ladder A's w in {2,4,8} cells cost roughly 3.75x their episode count in calls, so the 54-76h Tier 0 figure is understated by roughly 2-3x.
reviews.missing_baseline: The disjoint-episode, same-type instruction: I optimized on a pool of the same three task types that is disjoint from the pool used to distil B_own, run against B_own and B_oth (four cells at n=500 would do). This is the only arm that distinguishes 'the instruction absorbed the content of these specific episodes' from 'the instruction learned this task type's procedure from any episodes', and the container-substitution framing -- one training pool, two containers -- is exactly the thing it tests. A second, cheap omission: a hand-written type-specific instruction (a person given the task-type list, not the episodes) as the control for whether the optimizer is doing anything the type label alone does not, which matters because prediction 2 already asserts a large type-specific component.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is far above the norm for a proposal in process -- dated re-scan (2026-09-03 vs 2026-08-21), 15 queries over 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 IDs, a committed scan table with a stated no-additions rule, one competitor PDF read in full with its extracted text SHA256-committed, and a self-correction of a web snippet that misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 against the PDF's +3.6. It is not a rubber stamp: it withdraws a v2 novelty sentence and reinstates five wrongly retracted citations. But the state it reports is 'novelty not yet established', which is a weakness, not a neutral. Three obligations are explicitly undischarged, and they are the load-bearing ones: (2) the search for held-out-episode/data-provenance crossovers in the prompt-optimization, contamination and data-attribution literatures has *never been run*, and it bears on the single primitive the residual novelty rests on -- the proposal concedes that if it lands, the contribution 'reduces to the ALFWorld measurement, the on-policy control and the compiled-block comparison', which is a workshop paper; (1) the appendix of arXiv 2608.14036 is unopened and is named as the collision that would gut prediction 6, so one of eight falsifiable predictions is knowingly at risk of pre-emption; (3) the ALFWorld/embodied cross-task-type transfer literature has not been searched, and cross-type transfer of procedural memory is the most likely place the type-set manipulation already exists under another name -- it is also the literature that would tell the authors in advance whether G3 can pass. Verification is single-channel for everything except EvoAgentBench: arXiv is unreachable from the node, so the remaining ~25 IDs are confirmed through web-search snippets, the exact channel that already produced one documented factual error, and 'confirmed absent from the paper' claims (no token matching, no combined condition) are asserted from abstracts for every competitor but one. I cannot name a preprint that already makes this exact claim, and the closest one the authors did find (EvoAgentBench 2607.05202) they have correctly characterized as pre-empting the headline but not the interaction. The honest summary is that the novelty claim is conditional on searches that should have been run before the proposal was submitted for review, and reviewers will treat 'we claim no novelty for the primitive and have not looked' as an unresolved risk rather than as candor credit.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A 2x2 provenance crossover in ALFWorld in which both containers — a distilled experience bank and a GEPA-optimized instruction — are built from the same training episodes but labelled by which three of the six task types those episodes came from, so that 'how much of memory's value an optimizer already holds' is read off the instruction-provenance x bank-provenance interaction at matched test type, with a best-of-w sampling ladder subtracted as a headroom correction.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (2607.05202), which the proposal itself concedes already puts ReasoningBank (+3.6) and GEPA (+1.2) on the same 528/267 trajectories and therefore already publishes the qualitative headline 'an optimizer given the same episodes gets roughly what the bank gets.' What survives is the provenance labelling, the combined optimizer-plus-bank cells and the ALFWorld setting — i.e., an identification-and-quantification contribution on top of a published qualitative result, which caps how much this can be worth. Second threat is MIPROv2 (2406.11695): instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint optimization on one training set is the two-container ablation, and its finding that the split is task-dependent pre-empts the answer's shape. Third, and under-acknowledged: ExpeL (2308.10144) already stores its learned artifact as a natural-language 'insights' block distilled from training episodes and prepended to the prompt. That artifact is an instruction in all but name, so the paper's rhetorical claim ('memory is just an un-optimized prompt') is arguably instantiated inside the closest target system rather than discovered by this study — the proposal's own Related Work concedes GEPA and ExpeL 'run the same learning principle.'
reviews.strongest_objection: The claim threshold is arithmetically incompatible with the design's own gate, so the primary can fail while the hypothesis is true. Delta_abs = [Inner(I_oth) - Inner(I_own)] - ladder correction is bounded above by Inner(I_oth), and the only guarantee the design provides on that quantity is G3: the relevance advantage at I0 is >= 4pt (lower CI >= 1pt). Inner(I_oth) will if anything be smaller than Inner(I0), since I_oth is more accurate than I0 and the proposal's own argument is that accuracy compresses Inner multiplicatively. So Delta_abs >= 5pt requires Inner(I_oth) > 5pt AND Inner(I_own) ~ 0 (essentially total absorption) AND a near-zero ladder correction, all at once. A study that passes G3 at 4-6pt and then finds a genuine 60-70% absorption produces Delta_abs ~ 2-3pt, below the stated MDE of 4.6-4.8pt, and is reported as inconclusive. The proposal never reconciles Prediction 2 (relevance advantage >= 4pt) with Prediction 1 (Delta_abs >= 5pt); as written they are close to mutually exclusive. Compounding this: (a) Ladder A is not information-free with respect to the quantity it corrects — committing to the modal admissible action over w samples mechanically attenuates the leverage of any injected text on the committed action, so Inner_H declines with w for prompt-sensitivity reasons rather than headroom, and Ladder B (step budget) shares no such mechanism, so agreement between the two ladders does not validate the fit and disagreement does not localize the fault. (b) The mechanism rule has no bucket for the most likely confound. B_oth is an active distractor (off-type procedures against a templated ALFWorld goal), so Inner is partly harm-driven, and a stronger on-type instruction is plausibly more robust to distracting text; that produces a break deficit under I_own, which the pre-registered 2/3 rule (fix deficit -> absorption, break excess -> interference) routes to 'mixed' rather than flagging as the alternative explanation it is. Distractor-robustness and content absorption are not separated anywhere in the Tier 0 grid.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Promote the scale-free absorbed share, 1 - Inner(I_own)/Inner(I_oth), from 'descriptive' to the confirmatory endpoint with a pre-registered threshold (e.g. >= 50% with a lower CI above 20%), and raise G3 from >= 4pt to >= 8-10pt so the ratio is estimable — a ratio endpoint is invariant to the size of the relevance advantage, which is exactly the unknown that currently decides whether the study can conclude anything. 2) Use the frontier reflector the track's resource section explicitly grants (a few hundred dollars for the optimizer/reflector role). A local 32B reflector is the choice that minimizes I1, minimizes absorption, and makes the G2 failure branch live; the proposal calls this conservative, but conservative here means designing for an effect below your own MDE. 3) Replace or supplement Ladder A with a level knob that does not change prompt sensitivity — e.g. an instruction optimized on a third, disjoint slice of episodes and titrated to matched accuracy, or off-type demonstration count — and add an explicit distractor-robustness control: a plausibly-worded, token-matched, task-irrelevant block run at BOTH I_own and I_oth. Cell 24 is the right object but it is Tier 1, single-instruction, and cuttable; promote it to Tier 0 and run it in both instruction cells. Add a break-deficit bucket to the mechanism rule. 4) Re-derive the compute arithmetic with the sampling and step multipliers: cell 10 is budgeted as 4,500 episodes x 15 calls = 67,500 calls, but best-of-w at w in {2,4,8} multiplies per-step calls, giving roughly 500 x 3 conditions x 15 steps x (2+4+8) = 315,000 calls — about a quarter of the entire stated 900,000-call Tier 0 budget from one cell, with the same error in cells 11 and 18. 5) Move I_all x {M0, B_all} on S_test into Tier 0 (see missing baseline).
reviews.missing_baseline: Two, both Tier 0 omissions. (i) I_all x {M0, B_all} on S_test — an instruction optimized on the whole pooled training set against the whole pooled bank, i.e. the configuration a practitioner actually deploys. Every square cell uses an instruction optimized on 500 games of three task types, so Prediction 5's headline practitioner number ('at an instruction optimized on the same episodes, the bank stops paying') is measured for a half-data, type-restricted optimizer run and is checked in the deployment configuration only at Tier 1 on the 274-game official splits (cell 20), which is cuttable and underpowered at n=274. (ii) A 2-shot expert-trajectory ReAct baseline as an alternative I0. The published ALFWorld results the proposal leans on for its '5-15 point' memory effects were obtained under scaffolds containing in-context expert trajectories; I0 here is a hand-written instruction with the demonstration slot empty. G1 (memory must gain >= 5pt at I0) becomes easier the weaker I0 is, and the paper's whole thesis is that the gain was an artifact of an unfilled instruction slot — which makes the choice of I0 the single most outcome-determining unmeasured design decision in the study. Without a demonstration-bearing I0, outcome (v) (the demonstration slot is the whole story) cannot be distinguished from absorption, and cell 16 (J) alone does not fix this because J is only run at the optimized instruction, not as an alternative baseline scaffold.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is well above the norm and I credit it: dated scans (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), 15 queries over 244 papers, 54 by-id abstract verifications, PDF-level verification of the closest work with a committed extracted-text SHA256, an explicit retraction/reinstatement log for five IDs wrongly dropped in v2, and a self-caught numerical correction (a web snippet's +7 for ReasoningBank corrected to +3.6 from the PDF). That is a real search, not a gesture. But it does not establish novelty, for three reasons the proposal itself states. First, arXiv is unreachable from the node and Semantic Scholar was rate-limited, so every 'confirmed absent' claim except the EvoAgentBench one rests on a single web-search channel; negative claims from a single channel are the weakest kind. Second, three pre-freeze obligations are undischarged and one of them — targeted search for held-out-episode and data-provenance crossovers in the prompt-optimization, contamination and data-attribution literatures — targets precisely the primitive the contribution rests on. The proposal is candid that if that search hits, the contribution reduces to the ALFWorld measurement, the on-policy control and the compiled-block comparison; a reviewer must score the proposal as submitted, and as submitted the core novelty claim is conditional on a search that has never been run. Third, obligation (1), the unopened appendix of 2608.14036, is the collision that would gut Prediction 6. I cannot name a preprint that already runs this exact provenance square — but my knowledge does not extend past most of the 2026 IDs cited, so I am relying on the proposal's own record, and by that record the strongest nearby result (EvoAgentBench's optimizer-vs-bank table on shared trajectories) is already published, which means even a clean scan leaves this as an identification-and-quantification paper rather than a new finding. Under the venue's own rule that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this costs the submission roughly a point of novelty even though the check itself is honest and unusually diligent.
